verdict.rationale: Orama's docs recommend `insertMultiple` for large record sets. It inserts in configurable batches (default 1000) and avoids blocking the event loop, so bulk import is a documented first-party capability. Nothing in the evidence shows throughput at millions-of-documents scale, and there is no async task or job tracking to signal when indexing completes. missing for 10: async indexing task/job status tracking or completion notification, evidence of import performance at millions-of-documents scale, a documented Cloud bulk-ingestion API (the REST APIs are private), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can bulk-import millions of documents quickly, with async task tracking to know when indexing completes

citations.quote: If you have a lot of records, we suggest using the insertMultiple function... You can pass a third, optional, parameter to change the batch size (default: 1000).
Inserting a large number of documents in a loop could potentially block the event loop. Instead `insertMultiple` handles this case better.
